headline: The aerobic-efficiency trend holds as volume plateaus, with strength frequency doubling into a genuinely durable base a month out from St. Olavsleden.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The picture continues to point in one direction: your engine is settling. Comparable easy efforts keep landing at lower heart rates, and this week's short easy runs sat right in that lower band without any sign of drift. This isn't a single good session anymore — it's a consistent, weeks-long pattern that now reads as a real efficiency gain rather than day-to-day variance.

What's more notable today is that your strength frequency has doubled versus the prior block while running volume has held essentially flat and Zone 2 time has stayed high. That combination — maintained aerobic time on feet plus meaningfully more strength work — is exactly the durability profile a self-supported, pack-loaded, multi-day crossing rewards. You're building resilience without inflating running load, which is the sustainable version of getting ready.

With the crossing now roughly a month out, the base looks broad rather than sharp, and that suits the demand. The one gap worth naming honestly is specificity: the recent runs remain flat and pack-free, so the aerobic and strength gains haven't yet been translated into the exact terrain and load you'll face.
watch_items: Whether pack-loaded or back-to-back sessions start appearing to bridge the gap between general base and the specific demand of the crossing.
Whether per-run elevation begins climbing to rehearse the sustained up- and downhill of the border mountain section.
Whether the doubled strength frequency is held or deliberately eased as event-specific durability work takes priority.
The sleep signal has been erratic across tracked nights — worth watching whether it stabilises as volume and strain hold steady.

evidence_items.text: ▼ Easy-run HR averaging 142 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 10 vs 7 runs)
▲ 4-week volume 144 km vs 133 km prior block (+8%)
▲ Zone 2: 258 min vs 180-240 min/week target (143% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 1.5%
▬ Strain:tolerance ratio 0.93 (MAINTAINING) (strain 72, tolerance 77); sleep averaging 7h37m over the same period
